follow-up time: Up to birth, with mention of the need for longer follow-up
exposure: Nucleoside analog therapy in fathers prior to pregnancy
cohort: 201 couples with fathers positive for HBV markers (case group) and 188 couples with fathers positive for HBV markers and mothers negative for HBsAg (control group)
finding: Nucleoside analog therapy in fathers with HBV prior to pregnancy was associated with a significant reduction in father-to-infant HBV vertical transmission.
mod_finding: No statistically significant differences in delivery mode were observed between infants born to fathers who did or did not receive nucleoside analog therapy prior to pregnancy.
